epic.title: Visual recording on the Go-first AgentReel UX
epic.goal: Extend the areel-ux implementation with compact, continuously written visual-state recordings and an indexed event timeline. Preserve its Go-owned GUI, Live/History navigation, checkpoint helper and export orchestration; support days of recording, independent scrub-back and fixed-cutoff course-video export across tens of terminals, with truthful timing and best-effort fidelity warnings.

notes: Approved epic already materialized; do not resubmit or recreate it. After the user merged areel-ux, they explicitly approved the reviewed plan corrections and beginning work. Baseline ef32a76c604da157c318aaa17b1df4585fa7491f contains the finished Go application, four thin adapters, unmodified player and existing raw history/export stack; no further integration is needed. V0 now reconciles documentation, ownership and matching-source validation evidence (docs/visual-recording-baseline.md). This JSON records the approved plan revision; runtime statuses and refinements live in the existing Frontloop tasks. Promote only the next prerequisite-satisfied task; no blanket readiness. V4 owns new-format activity and Pi sender/receiver lifetime-cap changes; V7 owns remaining v1 2506 recipes/speed/chapters/marker handoff. Older activity/v1 acceptance and change identities remain intact, with no automatic completion or duplicate writer. Reuse the existing Go UX, native avt 0.18 helper and Go Chromium/FFmpeg jobs; no frontend rebuild, vendor patch or second emulator. New recordings prioritize supported visual footage; continue on detected unsupported visuals with explicit fidelity-incomplete intervals, not raw fallback or concealed parser/storage failures. Old raw archives/readers remain. Preserve exact/estimated/unknown timing: default exports use verified durable coverage; any estimated-tail export needs separate approval. Tests use private fixtures, not working recordings. No installation, activation, archive migration/deletion, keylogging, prompt-body/tool-argument metadata, auth expansion or Resolve operations. Fable 5.1's local-CLI review of the original draft remains recorded in docs/visual-recording-frontloop-review.md; it is not a claimed second review of this revision. Read-only post-merge review 705a3547-c4b9-414c-84a9-09220ec74a23 verified the plan corrections and matching-source Nix evidence.
risks: The UX merge is complete. Remaining overlap must follow docs/visual-recording-baseline.md ownership; do not re-integrate, resurrect removed controllers, or automatically complete older tasks.
Asciicast deltas and holder receipt times do not currently establish exact idle coverage. A healthy process, ALiS Init, dump acknowledgement or wall-clock heartbeat alone is not a source barrier.

The native helper/recorder uses avt 0.18.0; the pinned player 3.17.0 embeds avt 0.16.0. Existing continuation tests are valuable but do not establish canonical visual-store or unsupported-feature fidelity.

The official player has no public grid importer. Qualify a minimal shared presentation adapter before committing the schema; do not fork the vendor bundle or silently introduce a second product renderer.

Best-effort capture can permanently omit unsupported visuals after raw input is discarded. Warning detection cannot reveal source information never emitted by the watch stream; downstream uncertain interpretation must not be cleared without evidence.

SQLite/WAL, driver packaging with CGO_ENABLED=0, checkpoint behavior, event durability and recovery are new work. Long read transactions can pin WAL growth; content checksums and recoverable publication boundaries must remain explicit.
Existing history/export still reconstruct raw casts and carry request/job caps; those are not day-scale guarantees. Storage savings do not remove terminal parsing CPU or video encoding cost.
Actual Zellij capture/resize readiness remains independently unqualified. Synthetic success cannot waive that existing rollout gate or authorize working capture.

Dense new visual content and semantic events must still consume storage. No fixed storage/capacity or frame-perfect physical-terminal guarantee is made without a measured workload and supported-feature contract.

tasks.title: V0 — Reconcile merged baseline and remaining scope
tasks.goal: Record the already-merged Go-first baseline, matching-source test evidence and approved remaining ownership. Reconcile documentation without repeating integration or rebuilding the GUI.
acceptanceCriteria: Record merged baseline ef32a76c604da157c318aaa17b1df4585fa7491f and the user's approval to update the plan and begin; no additional integration or rewriting of existing changes.

Confirm the combined tree has the Go catalog/viewer/activity/marks, warm live ownership, preview caches, immutable history cutoffs, native avt helper, and CLI/browser export integration; no code-copy/recommit or unrelated workspace changes.

Reconcile CONTEXT.md, implementation/proposal HTML and relevant docs, including ACTIVITY.md 1024/8 MiB versus source 8192/16 MiB. Assign new-format activity/Pi capacity to V4 and remaining v1 2506 recipe/marker handoff to V7; preserve older acceptance, original payload identity, raw inspection and retention contracts without automatically completing siblings.

Persist matching filtered-source provenance for prior Nix browser/video/race logs, including warm restart and export boundaries. Distinguish prior passing evidence from tests run now and Go equality from unverified helper/Nix equality. No installed services or working recordings are touched.
designDecisions: Use areel-ux as the implementation baseline, not a competing frontend or export stack.
Go continues to own application logic, HTML, contracts, timing, jobs and tests; thin browser adapters and the pinned renderer remain presentation infrastructure.
Graph integration and capture/rollout permissions are separate from plan approval.
tasks.implementationNotes: Dependency: none; reconcile baseline and ownership before V1. User confirmed the merge and approved beginning work. docs/visual-recording-baseline.md owns evidence/scope mapping. Runtime queue status is authoritative; do not repeat integration.

tasks.title: V1 — Specify source clocks and visual presentation boundaries
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V0 reconciliation; UX integration and permission to begin are settled. Estimated-tail export is excluded unless separately approved; default exports remain within verified durable coverage.
tasks.goal: Define and demonstrate the clock and presentation contract that lets a visual archive hold unchanged screens while retaining honest event positions, durable endpoints and export cutoffs. Establish this with fixtures before freezing the storage format.
acceptanceCriteria: Specify source, received, durable and estimated frontiers, common clock mapping, sequence order, timestamp representation/precision, placement uncertainty and half-open interval semantics; do not equate wall-clock health or ALiS IDs with archival coverage.

Fixtures cover long true silence, repeated unchanged redraws, delayed FIFO delivery, queued input, equal timestamps, producer clock differences, monotonic/wall-clock changes, pause/resume, natural completion, crash and late arrivals after an export cutoff.

Prove an idle coverage/clock mechanism at the capture boundary or complete V1 with a usable degraded contract: retain the last verified source/durable frontier; display trailing holds and beyond-frontier event placement only as explicitly estimated or unknown with receipt basis and uncertainty. Export defaults to verified durable coverage; any estimated-tail extension requires a separately approved explicit opt-in and permanent manifest/UI labelling. Record the missing source mechanism and follow-up remedy without blocking unrelated storage/GUI work or falsely claiming exact coverage. Receipt fits, dump acknowledgements and heartbeats alone are not source barriers.

Define rendering boundaries for fragmented UTF-8/escapes, zero-delta ordering, synchronized updates, resize and visible cursor changes. Default to interpreting and comparing after every source event on its original clock; record changed visual states while preserving same-time order. No positive-duration state is omitted by debounce/quantization. Any coalescing policy needs V2 cost/fidelity evidence and explicit operator approval before V5 enables it.

Events during unchanged holds remain navigable with honest precision; paused/unobserved time is not invented footage; late source or metadata cannot retroactively modify a frozen export. Document source capability gaps and test limits.
designDecisions: Media time and operator wall-clock display are separate; edit/export uses an explicit integer/rational time representation with documented source precision.
A visually unchanged terminal is not stalled solely because it produces no new screen record.
Existing approximate anchors stay labelled as such; no implicit precision upgrade for legacy data.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V0. Extend current archive validator/footageClock contracts and synthetic test harnesses. Paths: internal/reel/{capture_unix.go,holder.go,activity.go}, internal/archive/format.go, live checkpoint provenance. Changes to capture ownership or source protocol outside the agreed scope must be brought back with evidence rather than patched around.

tasks.title: V2 — Extend the existing avt helper with canonical visual readout
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V1 presentation/clock contract; the finished UX and helper are the established baseline.
tasks.goal: Reuse the packaged avt 0.18.0 helper to expose bounded visible rows and presentation metadata while retaining full hidden state in memory. Prove a shared rendering path for those views before committing to the production visual schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend the existing framed helper API and Go owner with bounded canonical visible-state readout; preserve F/R/D/Q continuation behavior and its tests. Do not hash full Vt::dump checkpoints as visual equality.

Specify canonical cells/graphemes and widths, attributes, default/indexed/RGB color and palette semantics, geometry, visible cursor shape/visibility and supported overlays. Hidden cursor movement, pen changes and parser state do not create new visible states unless they affect presentation.

Differential tests cover unchanged full redraws with arbitrary input fragmentation, typing/scrolling, Unicode/wide/combining glyphs, palette/style changes, blink/cursor, resize, primary/alternate screens and partial sequences; compare rendered results as well as cell models.

Prove BOTH helper visual readout and renderer parity before V2 completes or V3 freezes the schema. First candidate: deterministic canonical-state ANSI repaint into a reset unmodified official player, followed by bounded row-diff presentation events; reuse existing checkpoint Init/segmented contracts without replaying discarded raw history. Validate widths, palettes, styles, cursor and supported animation semantics at render time. No vendor patch or second independent renderer; if this bridge fails, keep V2 blocked and request review of the evidenced alternative.

Detected unsupported visual features continue supported capture and open explicit fidelity-incomplete intervals. Repeated warnings remain sparse; unknown upstream omissions are not claimed detectable. Stateful uncertainty remains until an evidenced recovery condition.

Benchmark per-event helper readout and a changed-rows readout where available at 1/10/32 instances, including dense output and round-trip overhead. Record pinned source/Cargo evidence for recorder/helper 0.18 and player 0.16 (player gitHead 8ba9c54008ed1f25d2914abe31ea118dbf7da2e4); do not rely solely on manifest version or diagnostic strings. Preserve Go-owned orchestration, no browser-per-recorder or speculative shared daemon.
designDecisions: Extend tools/avt-checkpoint and castexport.AVT instead of introducing another terminal engine.
New visual archives preserve supported presentation, not exact original cast bytes.
Best-effort fidelity warnings are not permission to hide parser/storage failures, silently drop supported changes, or collect raw fallback data.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V0 and V1 presentation contract. Reuse tools/avt-checkpoint/{src/main.rs,Cargo.lock}, internal/castexport/avt.go, reference player and existing Go browser continuation tests. The proof should be a small fixture-to-visual-view end-to-end path, not a second GUI.

tasks.title: V3 — Implement the transactional visual archive and snapshots
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V1 plus BOTH V2 engine and renderer proofs; do not freeze the schema on partial qualification.
tasks.goal: Store reusable visual content and timed references in a private SQLite/WAL database per recording. Provide bounded indexed reads and immutable snapshot selections while capture appends.
acceptanceCriteria: Select/pin one maintained packaging-compatible SQLite binding, retaining CGO_ENABLED=0 for the ordinary package unless a separate reviewed change is needed. Test the same driver in ordinary builds and CGO_ENABLED=1 race checks, without build-tag driver substitution. Update Go/Nix closure/license evidence; no runtime downloads.

Use an explicitly identified new schema: compressed canonical row payloads, complete row-reference screen definitions, timed presentation records, segment/clock/fidelity metadata and progress. Preserve existing raw archive readers unchanged; do not reinterpret their inert legacy version field.

Repeated identical views create no new visual payload or presentation record; one changed row reuses all unaffected rows. Cursor/animation metadata does not duplicate screen content. Per-recording dedup indexes live on disk with bounded caches and checked canonical equality.

Document transactions, checksums, reference/sequence integrity, decoded/work limits, commit batching and durable acknowledgements. Specify journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=FULL or an explicitly justified equivalent durability boundary. Require a supported local filesystem for separate holder-writer/library-reader processes; confine database/WAL/SHM/temp artifacts to owned 0700 private locations with 0600 files and bounded private/memory temp storage, never a shared raw spool. Finalized content is immutable; tiny hold/progress updates do not create endless files.

Define visual equivalents of durable/accepted progress, typed create/publish/backlog storage failure, RETENTION.md stored-byte and validated-duration warning bases, and completion identity/totals. Distinguish logical content, allocated database/WAL space and verified versus estimated duration; no quota/deletion policy change. Implement format-aware read-only doctor/verification and explicitly scoped separate-destination salvage of independently verified recoverable records, never in-place repair or invented completeness.

Snapshot selections freeze visual/event cutoffs, hold endpoints, fidelity and clock interpretation. Concurrent append and late events cannot alter them. Readers use bounded short transactions rather than pinning a WAL reader for a whole export.

Crash/publication-boundary, ENOSPC, slow sink, corruption/missing reference and cancellation tests demonstrate truthful durability, bounded recovery and no invalid frame exposure. Test interrupted partial WAL transactions retaining the acknowledged committed prefix, plus arbitrary committed-WAL damage that must be detected/refused rather than claimed recoverable. Process-kill tests do not prove physical power-loss durability. Salvage only independently verified recoverable content; database transaction success is not a fidelity claim.

Cold late-time seeks do not scan/replay the whole source history. WAL/checkpoint tests with active readers and repeated idle progress show bounded working memory and stabilized transient storage rather than unbounded log retention.
designDecisions: SQLite/WAL per logical recording, zstd-compressed reusable rows and complete row-reference states; no long delta dependency chain or cross-recording dictionary.
Old archives remain readable and unmodified. No automatic migration/deletion of old or active captures.
Capture, viewing and export are separate owners; source mutation is not required for reader snapshots.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V1–V2. Reuse snapshot cutoff semantics from internal/archive/snapshot.go, not its raw-frame representation. Define only the small source/snapshot seams required by old-raw and new-visual readers; avoid a speculative storage plugin framework.

tasks.title: V4 — Index durable activity on the visual recording timeline
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V1/V3. V0 records approved ownership of new-format activity/Pi changes; no concurrent legacy writer or rewriting of original payloads.
tasks.goal: Preserve existing metadata ingress and attribution while removing the fixed holder-lifetime event cap. Link agent, user and lifecycle events to visual holds and segments without inferring missing identities or timing.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a format-selected indexed activity sink without rewriting historical sidecars or disrupting the legacy writer. Persist new-format identities/order/dedup rather than an unbounded RAM table or receiver 8192-record/16 MiB lifetime cap. After V0 assigns Pi ownership, also remove/replace its matching per-binding lifetime admission cap for the new format using bounded queue/rate/in-flight policies; test beyond both old limits end-to-end. Keep bounded envelopes/handlers, explicit overload accounting and accepted-versus-durable receipts.

Preserve actual declared producer/agent/conversation/parent/location provenance and unknown visibility; retried identical IDs remain idempotent across supported recovery, while conflicting payloads reject. Continue reading historical sidecars without rewriting them.

Use the V1 clock mapping for events during idle holds, rendering, pause/resume and interrupted tails. Unknown or estimated anchors remain explicit; metadata admission does not advance visual source coverage or falsely certify recording health.

Start from pi/agent-reel/README.md's existing hook table; mark requested user-submission/panel actions implemented, metadata-only-possible or excluded. Any scoped adapter changes require V0's Pi2504 ownership mapping and metadata-only behavior. Do not infer semantic actions from screen differences or promise native terminal selection/mouse overlays absent from capture.
No raw keylogging, prompt/response bodies or tool-argument metadata collection is added. Render labels/data as untrusted text; event activity can grow while visual content remains unchanged.

Tests exceed prior lifetime caps with bounded memory and verify concurrent producers, retries, reordered timestamps, gaps, pagination and export event-cutoff stability. Existing Go marks/activity presentation contracts remain covered.
designDecisions: Activity events and visual changes are independent tracks with an explicit timing relationship.
Disk history can grow with meaningful events; queue/resource bounds must not masquerade as retention deletion.
Use the existing Go application and Pi ingress surfaces, not a second event model in browser code.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V1/V3. Approved ownership: V4 owns the new-format indexed sink, Pi sender and receiver lifetime-cap changes, and scoped metadata-only hooks. Preserve original activity-foundation2500/v1 2503/2504 acceptance and payload identities; do not rewrite legacy work or complete siblings automatically. Coordinate holder.go with V5. Follow Pi docs before adapter changes; see docs/visual-recording-baseline.md.

tasks.title: V5 — Wire continuous visual capture into the existing holder
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V1–V3. V4 is not a capture prerequisite; coordinate overlapping holder files before concurrent work.
tasks.goal: Connect the qualified terminal readout and transactional visual writer to existing capture ownership, keeping capture independent of GUI/export consumers. Establish the new path in isolated fixtures before default rollout.
acceptanceCriteria: Reuse backend binding, holder ownership, FIFO/lifecycle, pause/resume/stop/interruption and supervision. For NEW visual recordings, the visual writer replaces archive.Archive as the sole durable sink: no raw archive is also written. Wire V3's typed create/publish/backlog failures, watchdog, Stats-equivalent progress/retention warnings, format-aware completion marker/record and doctor/verification/salvage paths; absent clean completion remains incomplete. Capture works without the GUI; no working recordings are restarted, modified or converted.

Interpret every supported source instruction and persist only changes according to V1/V2. Hold/progress updates retain honest idle duration and fidelity status; no hidden raw duplicate is retained except explicitly scoped diagnostic fixtures.

Keep existing recorder-owned live stream usable for supported captures during transition, with provisional live state distinct from durable visual coverage. Never splice ALiS IDs/checkpoints into the archive clock without proof or silently fall back to historical replay labelled Live.

Bound queues, geometry, readout work and disk batching per target. Slow/closed GUI readers or export jobs cannot backpressure capture through unbounded queues; capture failure is visible and isolated. Count existing warm recorder engines when measuring added helper CPU/RAM.

Synthetic owned-resource tests cover unchanged output, true idle, active updates, resize, lifecycle controls, missing helper, unsupported visuals, slow/full storage, reader disconnect, recorder failure and crash recovery. Full hidden engine state stays runtime-only; resume requires a qualified fresh initialization.
Default activation remains gated by V8/V10; old running holders and raw readers remain supported. Changes do not imply complete real Zellij or macOS capture qualification.
designDecisions: One visual recorder per backend-qualified target, not per agent; no browser-per-terminal or new multiplexing daemon by default.
Continue supported capture with explicit fidelity-incomplete intervals, but classify actual unusable-parser/storage failures honestly.
No source event suppression as an optimization unless the qualified interpretation/presentation contract proves it safe.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V1–V3; V4 and V5 join at V6. Extend capture_unix.go and holder progress with format-selected durable sinks; preserve simultaneous file/stream UX for legacy captures. Coordinate shared holder.go ownership if V4 runs concurrently. RETENTION.md and completed storage-warning requirements are regression contracts, not permission to invent quotas. Measure total pipeline cost.

tasks.title: V6 — Feed visual history into the existing Go GUI
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V2 presentation proof and V3–V5. Preserve the finished four-adapter GUI, not a new frontend.
tasks.goal: Keep the areel-ux application and visual polish while adding new-format current previews, bounded historical navigation and fidelity-aware events. Live position and the user's viewing position remain independent.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain Go-rendered catalog/viewer, workspace identity/colors, filtering/grouping, duration semantics, activity/marks and existing focus/player ownership behavior. Domain state stays in Go; browser code is a thin presentation adapter.

Dispatch explicitly by format: old raw history stays readable; new visual history uses indexed bounded states without BuildHistory prefix replay. First projection target is the existing segmented route/player contract (bounded windows, no idleTimeLimit), with canonical initial repaint and row-diff ANSI presentation events from V2. Preserve window/event/work bounds and thin-adapter ownership; if a limit is reached, subdivide within declared index budgets or refuse visibly, not silently widen limits or truncate. Any alternative renderer contract must pass V2 review.

Reuse shared cutoff binding, request admission, preview caches and cancellation patterns. Cache keys include presentation identity/font/theme/overlay state; bounded visible-card work does not create a permanent player/socket per terminal.

Opening ongoing recordings remains Live or clearly unavailable. Scrub-back, event navigation and reload preserve the selected historical cutoff/playhead while new capture continues; Return to Live is explicit.

Show freshness, last visual change, source/durable/estimated positions, pause gaps, and fidelity-incomplete intervals as distinct facts. An unchanged current thumbnail is not automatically stale; a warning cannot clear merely because more output arrived.

Go-driven real-browser tests cover late seeks, true idle/holds, event navigation, unchanged card refresh, stale callbacks, selection/filter preservation, partial errors and multiple viewers under bounded I/O. GUI rendering matches V2's shared presentation path.
designDecisions: Adapt data sources beneath the existing Go UX; do not rebuild the frontend or patch the official player bundle.
Legacy history/checkpoint code is compatibility infrastructure for existing archives, not the new visual store.
Use current areel-ux source and LIBRARY.md as evidence; stale progress prose is not a scope definition.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V3–V5 and V2 rendering gate. Keep the completed catalog/marks/player/viewer adapters, one short-lived renderer document per serial preview, warm restart, zero-duration boundaries, and all migrated safety invariants. Adapt the Go history/preview/activity/marks data sources; never restore retired controllers or fake-DOM tests. Preserve Go browser and asset/license checks.

tasks.title: V7 — Adapt existing export jobs to frozen visual snapshots
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V3–V6. Approved V0 scope mapping assigns remaining recipe/time-map/chapter/marker work from v1 2506 to V7 without weakening or automatically completing that task.
tasks.goal: Reuse the existing Go CLI/browser export pipeline to render selected visual-history ranges while capture continues. One source/edit mapping drives video frames, activity and chapter/provenance metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Reuse job admission/cancellation, fixed cutoff identity binding, private staging, no-overwrite publication, Chromium/FFmpeg ownership and optional video package. Existing raw/cast exports retain their original-versus-derived provenance.

Add a new-format immutable visual snapshot input instead of rebuilding redundant raw cast history. Export freezes content/event cutoffs, hold endpoints and clock/fidelity interpretation, releases long read transactions and continues using bounded reads while capture appends.

Use V2/V6's shared state-to-presentation projection for GUI and video. First reuse target is a bounded derived fixed cast of canonical initial/row-diff repaint events for the existing videoexport input, not reconstructed original instructions. SourceSHA256 for that cast is explicitly derived; retain visual snapshot/content/event cutoffs separately. If projection exceeds input limits, refuse honestly or bring back an incremental-input proposal, never replay or expand full source history by stealth. Go owns orchestration; no Node driver, vendor patch or second pixel renderer.

Define non-destructive source ranges and rational/integer speed/frame mapping shared by frame sampling, chapters and event metadata. Preserve pause/interruption gaps and unknown anchors; same-frame events retain their meanings; late events never alter an existing export.

Support explicit rendering recipes for output dimensions/framing/padding/font size and cursor presentation, preserving original terminal geometry unless a selected edit intentionally transforms it. Preflight readability/crop/fit, pin font/glyph behavior, and document bounds rather than promise arbitrary full-day video jobs.

Include fidelity-incomplete intervals in manifests and a visible export warning without silently baking a new overlay into footage. A derived cast, if offered for visual recordings, is explicitly non-byte-exact.

Tests decode H.264/ProRes frames, verify timing/chapters/provenance and repeatability of frozen recipes, demonstrate append-after-cutoff and continued capture during export, and cover cancel/failure cleanup, WAL stability and bounded memory/temp storage. Resolve application operations remain outside scope.
designDecisions: Keep internal/videoexport and library_exports job infrastructure; replace the new-format input/presentation seam, not the exporter product.
Compact recording size is separate from encoded movie size and rendering throughput.
All successful exports have an explicit durable coverage boundary and retained source/event provenance.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V3–V6. V7 owns remaining v1 2506 selection/speed recipes, rational/integer time map including fractional frame rates, chapters and stable-ID clip-relative resolve-markers.json handoff. Preserve all original2506 criteria (same-frame pause/resume meanings, omitted/unanchored events, multi-segment fixtures), not automatic sibling completion. Reuse existing Go job/video infrastructure and bounds; full-day movies and actual Resolve operations are not promised. See docs/visual-recording-baseline.md.

tasks.title: V8 — Qualify multi-day and many-terminal visual recording
tasks.reviewReason: Await completed V1–V7; actual-capture permissions remain separate. Prior matching-source Nix checks and raw-history fixtures do not qualify the new visual stack.
tasks.goal: Establish measured evidence for the combined visual recorder, Go GUI and exporter before default rollout. Preserve the old qualification boundaries instead of treating synthetic performance as proof of working-terminal fidelity.
acceptanceCriteria: Run a reproducible fixture matrix of unchanged repaint, true idle, dense scrolling/typing, spinner-heavy output, Unicode/styles, resize/alternate screen, fidelity warnings and metadata-heavy workloads at 1/10/32 independent targets.

Separate accelerated eight-hour/three-day logical timelines from a real sustained-runtime soak with stated duration and hardware. Record aggregate and per-target CPU/RSS, row/state/timeline/event storage slopes, transient/WAL growth, commit p99, live lag, cold/random seek latency, recovery time and export throughput under concurrent capture.

Establish explicit workload-specific pass/fail resource budgets from the early V2/V3 measurements before the final run; do not label estimates measured or silently change budgets to make results pass. Report total existing recorder+helper overhead.

Show unchanged visual content does not grow with repeated redraws or wall-clock duration, except bounded progress/transient storage and genuine metadata events. Demonstrate cold indexed seek without historical replay and no export-held WAL growth.

Exercise process crashes, dependency corruption, cancellation, ENOSPC/slow I/O, lost live capability and overloaded metadata/readers; validate honest gaps, continued unaffected targets and no falsely successful recording/export.

Run Go unit/vet/race, pinned native-helper, Go browser, capture fixture and video suites through existing sd/Nix surfaces. Keep legacy regression coverage until each behavior has an evidenced replacement; keep a source graph/tree and artifact report.

Actual backend readiness/resize/working-view qualification remains a separate existing gate; use only explicitly authorized isolated capture resources. If that gate or any day-scale/resource criterion remains unmet, report blocked rollout with evidence and required next input, not a reduced-scope success.
designDecisions: Best-effort unsupported visuals are labelled limitations, not a waiver of correctness for supported features.
Keep no automatic retention deletion, global quotas, background activation, auth expansion or unqualified platform claims.
A synthetic 61-hour segmented-cast fixture is prior evidence for the old reader, not acceptance of the new visual archive.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V1–V7 and operator permission for any actual capture beyond existing fixtures. Extend .sd/tasks.yaml, nix/checks.nix and existing Go browser/video/capture harnesses. No service restart, private live recording mutation or working-client focus/resize/input changes.

tasks.title: V9 — Decide whether measured spinner growth warrants loop encoding
tasks.goal: Treat exact recurring animation compression as a measured stretch goal, not a prerequisite or speculative codec. If justified and approved, compress repeated state/timing patterns while preserving seeking and interrupted tails.
tasks.reviewReason: Requires V8 evidence of material timed-reference overhead and an explicit go/no-go decision before adding a loop codec. Ordinary row/state reuse is already required by the core plan.
acceptanceCriteria: Report content versus timing-reference growth for representative throbber workloads and the expected incremental savings/complexity; obtain a go/no-go decision.
If approved, bound pattern size, detection memory and expansion work; match whole relevant visual states and observed timing, with jitter preserved as residuals or ordinary non-loop records.

Verify exact duration/order, cycle-phase seeking, source/event mappings, resize/divergence breaks, crash publication and partial final tails. Never predict unobserved repeats or omit changing text outside a spinner region.
If not justified, document deferral and retain the simpler content-reused timed-reference path without weakening core capacity requirements.
designDecisions: Defer loop encoding until measurements justify it; no region masking or nominal-period timing substitution.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V8. Optional and not a prerequisite for V10 if core capacity passes. Approval of the main visual architecture does not automatically approve a speculative loop format.

tasks.title: V10 — Approve operator rollout of the qualified visual writer
tasks.goal: Approve and execute a scoped transition for new recordings only after source/backend and visual-stack qualification. Keep installed configuration, active captures, old archives and retention under operator control.
questions: After V8 and the existing backend capture gates pass, which explicit install/profile/service changes and new-capture default switch are authorized? Existing running recordings and archive conversion remain excluded unless separately requested.
acceptanceCriteria: Record completed qualification evidence and explicit rollout authorization, affected package/profile/service paths, rollback plan and limits; no activation is inferred from successful builds or this proposal.
Switch only approved new captures to the visual format; preserve active old holders and existing raw archives/readers. No automatic backfill conversion, deletion, restart or raw fallback.

Document supported visual/event features, exact/estimated/unknown timing, default durable export coverage, best-effort warnings, backend/platform limits, resource budgets, export recipes and visual-format doctor/verification/salvage support and limits.
Verify approved operational state with read-only checks and operator-controlled new-capture evidence. Failed rollout remains visible and reversible without rewriting the historical library.
designDecisions: Rollout is a separate operator gate; optional V9 is not required if the qualified baseline meets the core goals.
tasks.implementationNotes: Depends on V8 and the existing v1 real-capture and choose-the-private-library-and-approve-operator-activation gates. V10 records visual-writer-specific rollout criteria within that same operator authorization, not a parallel or weaker approval path. Coordinate mono/nix/Jack ownership only if separately authorized; generated Niri include remains user-owned. No auth change or Resolve mutation.
